summary: Traffic redirected to degraded model variant after canary throttling during dedicated capacity burst
description:
Issue summary:
During a customer traffic surge against their dedicated pool, a canary throttle event caused the orchestrator to move traffic away from the normal model variant into a degraded quantized variant instead of the configured higher-capacity fallback. Impact: customer observed variable outputs and ~2.2x token latency increase for 80% of requests over a 22-minute window.

Impact:
- ScaleApps reported elevated error rates and latency spikes affecting their chat product.
- A subset of requests returned responses from the quantized variant that produced shorter outputs and tokenization mismatches.
- No billing discrepancy reported, but customer-facing SLAs were breached for 18 minutes.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated-44) in us-east, running 4 x A100-equivalent nodes.
- Canary rollout of redwood-7b-v2 -> redwood-7b-quantized-v2 was in progress with traffic weighting 5% -> 95%.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Synthetic burst simulated by customer at 13:12 UTC (replay dataset attached in support ticket).
2) Orchestrator applied canary throttle policy due to observed per-node token processing lag.
3) Edge routing service routed sessions to fallback group; policy should have chosen warm-hot variant (redwood-7b-v2-warm) but instead selected quantized variant group.
4) Requests returned shorter completions and an increased per-token latency median.

Logs / Observations:
- Edge-proxy logs show header X-Route-Variant: quantized-v2 for affected sessions.
- Orchestrator metrics: canary_throttle_rate spiked to 0.42, batch_queue_depth increased.
- Serving runtime traces show kernel selection falling back to int8 path for variant grouped as "fallback-quantized".
- No node OOM or GPU eviction events reported.

Attachments:
- sample request/response pairs (anonymized)
- edge logs snippets (13:10 - 13:40 UTC)
- orchestrator telemetry graphs link

2026-03-10 13:41 UTC - Ben Foster (SRE): Initial triage - canary throttle triggered by sustained queue depth on two nodes. Observed that route selection favored a quantized fallback group. Investigating route-controller state and cache TTLs.

2026-03-10 14:05 UTC - Marina Li (Platform): Found stale fallback-mapping in route-controller snapshot; last snapshot apply at 12:58 UTC. Canary policy whitelist incorrectly mapped to fallback-quantized group for dedicated pools with tag 'burst-safe=false'.

2026-03-10 15:10 UTC - Ben Foster (SRE): Temporary mitigation applied - forced route-controller refresh and pinned ScaleApps cohort to warm variant. Re-routed ~98% of live sessions back to expected variant. Monitoring for 30m.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: route-controller snapshot staleness caused wrong fallback group mapping under surge conditions.
Hypothesis 2: canary throttle logic prioritized available capacity groups by a fallback_score that mistakenly favored quantized groups when 'burst-safe' flag present.
Telemetry checked: route-controller apply timestamps, edge routing logs, orchestrator throttle metrics, serving runtime kernel path logs.

Partial finding: route-controller cache TTL was set to 5m; in a rapid update window a stale snapshot remained active due to leader-election lag. This allowed an older fallback mapping to be used until forced refresh.

Additional finding: fallback_score computation treated lower expected latency as higher preference; quantized variant had lower nominal latency in profiling but poorer quality, leading to incorrect selection during throttle.
Consequence: customer saw degraded outputs and latency; orchestration did not follow configured 'prefer-warm-over-quantized' policy.
resolution:
Immediate: forced route-controller snapshot refresh and pinned ScaleApps cohort to warm variant (redwood-7b-v2-warm). Applied temporary override to fallback scoring.
Permanent: merged fixes in route-controller to (1) reduce snapshot TTL jitter, (2) ensure fallback_score includes explicit customer-tier and quality_weight, (3) add a canary-safe flag that prevents quantized selection for dedicated pools. Two PRs merged: route-controller/pull/834 and serving-runtime/pull/2191.
Customer communication: incident summary, timeline, and goodwill credit provided.
Follow-ups: add runbook entry for forced snapshot refresh, add a monitoring alert when fallback_score differs from policy expected for >2 minutes.
